spans.s:
मण् मण्, cl. 1. P. मणति, ममाण, &c.,
to sound, murmur.

मणि, इस्, m. f. (usually m., said to be fr. rt. मण्,
Uṇādi-s.

; a form मणी, f., is also given),
[]
a jewel, gem, precious stone (especially a pearl, bead,
or other globular ornament); an ornament or amulet
in general; anything excellent of its kind (e. g.
खग-मणि, a jewel of a bird); a crystal [cf. काच-
म्˚]; a magnet, loadstone; glans penis; clitoris;
the fleshy excrescences or processes on the neck of a
goat; = मणि-भन्ध, the wrist; a water-pot (=
अलिञ्जर); N. of a Nāga; N. of a companion of
Skanda (associated with Su-maṇi in Mahā-bh. Śalya-
p. 2534); N. of a sage (in Mahā-bh. Sabhā-p. 442);
of a son of Yuyudhāna (in Hari-vaṃśa 9207; also
read तूणि); of a work (abridged from the full title
of Tattva-cintāmaṇi, q. v.); of a collection of magical
formulas; [cf. Gr. μάννος, μόννος; Lat. monile.]
—मणि-कण्ठ, अस्, m. the blue jay or roller bird;
N. of a Nāga.
—मणिकण्ठक, अस्, m. a cock.
—मणि-कर्ण, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, ‘jewel-eared,’
having an ornament of any kind (as a mark) on the
ear; (अस्), m., N. of a Śiva-liṅga in Kāma-rūpa;
(ई), f. = मणि-करणिका below.
—मणि-करणिका, f.,
N. of a sacred pool or tank in Benares much fre-
quented by pilgrims, (also written मणि-कर्णिकी);
of a daughter of Caṇḍa-ghoṣa.
—मणिकर्णिका-
महिमन्, आ, m. and मणिकर्णिका-स्तोत्र, अम्, n.,
N. of two works by Gaṅgā-dhara.
—मणिकर्णिका-
माहात्म्य, अम्, n., N. of the twenty-second chapter
of the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the Śiva-Purāṇa.
—मणि-
कर्णीश्वर (˚णी-ईश्˚), अस्, m., N. of a Śiva-liṅga at
Benares.
—मणिकर्णेश्वर (˚ण-ईश्˚), अस्, m., N.
of a Śiva-liṅga in Kāma-rūpa.
—मणि-काच, अस्, m.
the feathered part of an arrow.
—मणि-काञ्चन,
अस्, m., N. of a mountain (mentioned in Mahā-bhā-
rata Bhīṣma-p. 426).
—मणि-कानन, अम्, n. a
wood or grove containing jewels; the neck, throat
(as covered with jewels).
—मणि-कार, अस्, m. a
worker in precious stones, lapidary, jeweller; N. of
the author of the work called Maṇi; of the author
of the Nyāya-cintāmaṇi.
—मणि-कुट्टिका, f. [cf.
कुट्टक], N. of one of the Mātṛs attending on
Skanda.
—मणि-कुसुम, अस्, m., N. of a Jina.
—मणि-कूट, अस्, m., N. of a mountain in Kāma-
rūpa.
—मणि-कृत्, त्, m. = मणि-कार.
—मणि-
केतु, उस्, m., N. of a particular comet or meteor.
—मणि-गण, अस्, m. a multitude of pearls.
—मणि-
गुण-निकर, अस्, m. ‘a multitude of strings of pearls,’
a species of the Ati-śakkarī metre, four times
˘ ˘ ˘ ˘ ˘ ˘ ˘ ˘, ˘ ˘ ˘ ˘ ˘ ˘ ¯.
—मणि-ग्रीव, अस्, आ,
अम्, ‘jewel-necked,’ wearing a necklace; (अस्), m.,
N. of a son of Kuvera.
—मणि-चूड, अस्, m., N. of
a Vidyā-dhara; of a king of Sāketa-nagara (= रत्न-
चूड); of a Nāga.
—मणि-च्छिद्रा, f. ‘jewel-
holed,’ N. of two medicinal herbs; = मेदा.
—मणि-
जला, ‘having jewel-like water,’ N. of a river.
—मणि-तारक, अस्, m. ‘jewel-eyed’ [cf. तारक];
the Indian crane.
—मणि-दण्ड, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘jewel-
handled,’ having a handle adorned with jewels.
—म-
णि-दत्त, अस्, m., N. of a man.
—मणि-दर, अस्,
m., N. of a chief of the Yakṣas.
—मणि-दर्पण,
अस्, m. a mirror adorned with jewels or consisting of
jewels; N. of a work on music.
—मणि-दीधिति,
इस्, f., N. of a work (abridged from the full title
of Anumāna-maṇidīdhiti).
—मणिदीधिति-गूढार्-
थ-प्रकाशिका, f., N. of a commentary by Bhavā-
nanda Siddhānta-vāg-īśa on the Maṇi-dīdhiti (said
to be an epitome of the Dīdhiti).
—मणि-दीप or
मणि-दीपिक, अस्, m. ‘jewel-lamp,’ a lamp having
jewels.
—मणि-दोष, अस्, m. a flaw or defect in a
jewel.
—मणि-द्वीप, अस्, m. ‘jewel-island,’ N. of a
mythical island in the ocean of nectar; the hood of
the serpent Ananta.
—मणि-धनु, उस्, m. ‘jewel-
bow,’ a rain-bow; N. of a king, (also read मणि-
धान or मणि-धाण्य.)
—मणि-धनुस्, उस्,
n. ‘jewel-bow,’ a rain-bow.
—मणि-धर, अस्, आ,
अम्, having or wearing jewels or beads.
—मणि-
धान, see मणि-धनु above.
—मणि-नाग, अस्,
m., N. of a snake-demon; N. of a sacred bathing-
place.
—मणि-निर्यातन, अम्, n. the restitution of
a jewel.
—मणि-पद्म, अस्, m., N. of a Bodhi-
sattva.
—मणि-पर्वत, अस्, m. ‘jewel-mountain,’
N. of a mythical mountain.
—मणि-पाली, f. ‘jewel-
keeper,’ a woman who has charge of pearls &c., a
[]
female keeper of jewels.
—मणि-पुच्छी, f. ‘jewel-
tailed,’ having jewels &c. on the tail; [cf. मणि-
बाल.]
—मणि-पुर, अम्, n. = मणि-पूर.
—मणि-
पुष्पक, अस्, m., N. of the conch-shell of Saha-
deva (Bhagavad-gītā 1. 16).
—मणि-पुष्पेश्वर
(˚प-ईश्˚), अस्, m., N. of one of Śiva's attendants.
—मणि-पूर, अम्, n., N. of a town in Kaliṅga
(situated on the sea-shore and the residence of
Babhru-vāhana); the pit of the stomach or a mysti-
cal circle on the navel; (अस्), m. the navel; a sort
of bodice (worn by women and richly adorned with
jewels).
—मणिपूरक, अम्, n., N. of a mystical
circle on the navel.
—मणिपूर-पति, इस्, m., N.
of king Babhru-vāhana.
—मणिपूर-विभेदन,
अम्, n., N. of a jewel.
—मणिपूरेश्वर (˚र-ईश्˚),
अस्, m. = मणिपूर-पति; (also written मणिपु-
रेश्वर.)
—मणि-प्रदान, अम्, n., N. of the
thirty-fourth chapter of the Sundara-kāṇḍa of the
Rāmāyaṇa.
—मणि-प्रदीप, अस्, m. = मणि-दीप.
—मणि-प्रभा, f. ‘jewel-splendor,’ N. of a par-
ticular metre, the first line of which is ¯¯˘¯¯˘˘
¯˘¯¯ and the second, third, and fourth ˘¯˘¯¯
˘˘¯˘¯¯; of a lake.
—मणि-प्रवेक, a most
excellent jewel; [cf. प्रवेक.]
—मणि-बन्ध,
अस्, m. the fastening or putting on of jewels; the
wrist (as the place on which jewels are fastened); a
kind of metre, four times ¯˘˘¯˘¯˘˘ [cf.
मणि-मध्य]; N. of a mixed race.
—मणि-
बन्धन, अम्, n. the fastening on of jewels, a
string of pearls, an ornament of pearls; the part of
a ring or bracelet where the jewels are set; the wrist
or fore-arm from the wrist to the elbow.
—मणि-
बाल, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘jewel-tailed’ or having jewel-like
lumps on the tail, (according to Mahī-dhara on Vāja-
saneyi-saṃhitā
XXIV. 3

= मणि-शुद्ध-बाल or
मणि-वर्ण-केश.)
—मणि-बीज, अस्, m. ‘having
jewel-like or pearl-like seeds,’ the pomegranate tree.
—मणि-भद्र, अस्, m., N. of a king of the
Yakṣas (the tutelary deity of travellers and mer-
chants, probably another name for Kuvera); of a
Jina or Jaina teacher (= पूर्व-यक्ष); of a
brother of Kuvera; of a Śreṣṭhin; [cf. माणि-
भद्र.]
—मणिभद्रक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a
race (in Mahā-bh. Bhīṣma-p. 2099; also read पारि-
भद्रक); of a serpent-demon.
—मणि-भव,
अस्, m., N. of one of the five Dhyāni-Buddhas.
—मणि-भित्ति, इस्, f. ‘jewel-walled,’ N. of the palace
of the serpent-demon Śeṣa.
—मणि-भू, ऊस्, f. a
floor inlaid with jewels.
—मणि-भूमि, इस्, f. a floor
inlaid with precious stones; a mine of jewels; [cf.
कुट्टिम.]
—मणि-भूमिका, f. a floor inlaid with
jewels; (according to a Scholiast मणिभूमिका-
कर्मन् = कृत्रिम-पुत्रिका-निर्माण.)
—मणि-
मञ्जरी, f. rows of jewels or pearls; a species of
the Ati-dhṛti metre, four times ˘¯¯¯˘˘˘˘˘˘
¯¯˘¯˘˘¯˘¯.
—मणि-मण्डप, अस्, m. ‘jewel-
palace, crystal-palace,’ N. of the residence of Śeṣa
and of Nairṛta, the ruler of the south-west quarter.
—मणि-मण्डित, अस्, आ, अम्, set or studded with
jewels or pearls.
—मणि-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing
or adorned with jewels, jewelled; (आन्), m. the sun;
N. of a Yakṣa; of a servant of Śiva; of a Rakṣas;
of a Nāga; of a king (who was Vṛtra in a former
birth); of a mountain; of a place of pilgrimage;
(अती), f., N. of a town of the Daityas; of a river.
—मणि-मध्य, अम्, n., N. of a metre, four
times ¯˘˘¯¯, ¯˘˘¯.
—मणि-मन्थ, अस्, m.,
N. of a mountain; (अम्), n. = माणिमन्थ, rock-
salt.
—मणि-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, formed or consisting
of jewels, set or studded with gems, jewelled.
—म-
णिमय-भू, ऊस्, f. a floor made of gems, a jewelled
floor; (उवस्), f. pl. jewelled floors.
—मणि-महेश,
अस्, m., N. of a place of pilgrimage mentioned in
Raghu-nātha's Rasika-ramaṇa.
—मणि-माला, f. a
string of jewels or pearls, necklace of precious stones;
a circular impression left by a bite (especially in
amorous dalliance); lustre, splendor, beauty; epithet
of Lakṣmī; a kind of metre, four times ¯¯˘˘¯¯
¯¯˘˘¯¯.
—मणि-मिश्र, अस्, m., N. of the author
of the Nyāya-ratna.
—मणि-मुक्ता, f., N. of a
river.
—मणि-मेखल, अस्, आ, अम्, girdled with
[]
gems, surrounded by jewels.
—मणि-मेघ, अस्, m.,
N. of a mountain.
—मणि-यष्टि, इस्, m. f. a jewelled
staff or stick.
—मणि-रत, अस्, m., N. of a Bud-
dhist teacher; (perhaps for मणि-रथ or मनो-
रथ.)
—मणि-रत्न, अम्, n. a jewel, gem,
precious stone.
—मणिरत्न-मय, अस्, ई, अम्,
formed or consisting of jewels, jewelled.
—मणि-
रत्न-माला, f. ‘garland of jewels,’ N. of a philo-
sophical treatise ascribed to Śaṅkarācārya.
—मणि-
रत्न-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, containing jewels, jewelled.
—मणि-रथ, see मणि-रत.
—मणि-राग, अस्,
आ, अम्, ‘jewel-coloured,’ having the colour of a
jewel; (अस्), m. ‘jewel-colour,’ the colour of jewels;
a kind of metre, four times ¯˘¯˘˘¯˘˘¯¯;
(अम्), n. vermilion (= हिङ्गुल).
—मणि-राज, अस्,
m. ‘jewel-king, jewel-chief,’ (probably) a diamond
[cf. मणीन्द्र].
—मणि-राम, अस्, m., N. of an
author; of a commentator who lived in the begin-
ning of this century.
—मणि-लिङ्गेश्वर (˚ग-ईश्˚),
अस्, m., N. of one of the eight Vīta-rāgas.
—मणि-
वर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a merchant.
—मणि-वाल,
see मणि-बाल.
—मणि-वाहन, अस्, m. ‘jewel-
bearer,’ an epithet of Kuśāmba (in Mahā-bh. Ādi-p.
2363).
—मणि-विशेष, अस्, m. a kind of jewel; an
excellent jewel.
—मणि-वीज, अम्, n. a pomegranate.
—मणि-शङ्ख-शर्कर, अस्, आ, अम्, having jewel-
like shells and gravel.
—मणि-शर = मणि-सर.
—मणि-शिला, f. a jewelled slab.
—मणि-शृङ्ग,
अस्, m. (probably) N. of the sun.
—मणि-शैल, अस्,
m. ‘jewel-mountain,’ N. of a mountain.
—मणि-
श्याम, अस्, आ, अम्, dark-blue like a jewel, i. e. like
a sapphire; (according to a Scholiast मणि = इन्द्र-
नील.)
—मणि-सर, अस्, m. a string of pearls, an
ornament of pearls, a necklace, (wrongly written
मणि-शर.)
—मणि-सार, N. of a work.
—मणि-
सूत्र, अम्, n. a string of pearls.
—मणि-सोपान,
अम्, n. steps or stairs set with jewels, a jewelled
staircase; a staff or stick set with jewels (?).
—मणि-
स्कन्ध, अस्, m., N. of a snake-demon.
—मणि-
स्तम्भ, अस्, m. a post or column set with jewels,
a jewelled post or pillar.
—मणि-स्रज्, क्, f. a garland
of jewels.
—मणि-हर्म्य, अम्, n. a jewelled palace,
crystal-palace; N. of a particular palace.
—मणीन्द्र
(˚णि-इन्˚), अस्, m. ‘jewel-chief,’ (probably) a diamond
[cf. मणि-राज].
—मणीश्वर-तीर्थ (˚णि-ईश्˚),
अम्, n., N. of a sacred bathing-place.
—मण्य्-आलोक,
N. of a commentary by Jaya-deva Tarkālaṅkāra on
part of the Tattva-cintāmaṇī, (also called आलोक.)
—मण्यालोक-कण्टकोद्धार (˚क-उद्˚), अस्, m.
‘removing thorns from the Maṇy-āloka,’ N. of a
commentary on the Maṇy-āloka.
मणि मणि. See p. 730, col. 2.

मणिक, अस्, m. a jewel, gem, precious stone;
(अस्, अम्), m. n. a water-jar or pitcher; (according
to Sāy.) globular formations of flesh on an animal's
shoulder; [cf. माणिक्य.]

माणिका माणिका, f. a particular weight,
= 2 Kuḍavas, = 1 Śarāva, = 8 Palas.

मणित, अम्, n. a murmuring sound, an inarticu-
late sound said to be uttered at cohabitation, murmur
libidinosum.

मणिल, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having fleshy excres-
cences (as on the dew-lap &c.).

मणीचक, अस्, m. a king-fisher, halcyon; (अम्),
n. a particular jewel, the moon-stone (probably a
sort of crystal; cf. चन्द्र-कान्त).

मणीय, Nom. A. मणीयते, &c., to become a
jewel.
मणीवक, अम्, n. a flower.

मण मण (fr. Arabic من a particular
measure of grain by weight = 40 ser, mentioned by
Hindū writers as used by the Turuṣkas or Muham-
madans, a ‘maund.’

माण माण, अस्, m. a species of plant (=
माणक).

मणऊ मणऊ (fr. Arabic منع), N. of the
seventh Yoga (in astronomy).

मणित्थ मणित्थ, अस्, m., N. of an astro-
nomer.

मण्टपी मण्टपी, f. a species of pot-herb
(= क्षुद्रोपोदकी).

मण्टि मण्टि, इस्, m., N. of a man; (pro-
bably wrongly for माण्टि.)

मण्ठ् मण्ठ्, cl. 1. A. मण्ठते, &c., to
desire eagerly, long for; to remember
with regret, to meditate sorrowfully, grieve for.

मण्ठ मण्ठ, अस्, m. a sort of baked
sweetmeat.

मण्ठक मण्ठक, a particular musical air;
[cf. प्रति-म्˚, मण्डक.]

मण्ड् मण्ड् (connected with rts. 2. मद्,
मन्द्), cl. 1. P. मण्डति, ममण्ड,
मण्डितुम्, to adorn one's self; cl. 1. A. मण्डते,
&c., to clothe, dress; to surround, encompass; to
divide, distribute; cl. 10. P. (ep. also A.) मण्ड-
यति (-ते), -यितुम्, to adorn; to rejoice, exhilarate;
[cf. Lat. mund-u-s, mund-are.]

मण्ड, अस्, अम्, m. n. (in Uṇādi-s. 1. 113. said
to be fr. rt. मन्), that part of any fluid which
rises and collects on the surface in the process of
fermentation or while boiling; the scum or thick
oily matter which forms on the surface of any liquor
or liquid; the thick part of milk, cream, (दधि-ज
मण्ड,) sour cream; cf. दधि-म्˚); the spirituous
part of wine, &c.; the scum of boiled rice (or any
grain); skimmings, scum, foam or forth in general;
barm, ferment; gruel; the best part of anything,
essence, pith (= सार); the head; (अस्), m. orna-
ment, decoration; the castor-oil tree, Ricinus Com-
munis [cf. अमण्ड]; a particular species of pot-
herb; a frog [cf. मण्डूक]; (आ), f. the emblic
myrobalan tree (= आमलकी); spirituous or vinous
liquor, brandy; (अम्), n. (Ved.) an oar (? connected
with मङ्ग).
—मण्ड-करण, अस्, m., N. of a
man; [cf. माण्डकर्णि.]
—मण्ड-चित्र, अस्, m.,
N. of a man; (आस्), m. pl. the family of Maṇḍa-
citra.
—मण्ड-प, अस्, आ, अम्, drinking the scum
of boiled rice or of any liquor, sipping cream, &c.;
(अस्, अम्), m. n. an open hall or temporary shed erected
on festive occasions, (in this sense probably fr. मण्ड,
an ornament, + 3. पा); a temple or building conse-
crated to a deity; a pavilion, shed, tent; an arbour,
bower; (अस्), m., N. of a man; (आ), f. a sort of pulse or
leguminous plant (= निष्पावी).
—मण्डप-क्षे-
त्र, अम्, n., N. of a particular sacred district.
—मण्-
डप-प्रतिष्ठा, f. the consecration of a temple.
—मण्ड-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made of cream or
from the scum of any liquid.
—मण्ड-हारक,
अस्, m. a distiller of spirits, &c.
—मण्डोदक (˚ड-
उद्˚), अम्, n. barm, yeast; the decorating of walls,
floors, &c. on festive occasions; = चित्त-राग, mental
excitement; (according to some) = चित्र-राग, varie-
gated colour.
माण्ड माण्ड, अस्, m., N. of a man.

मण्डक, अस्, इका, अम्, a sort of thick gruel
made of rice &c., (at the end of a comp., e. g.
प्रिय-मण्डक, fond of this dish); (अस्), m. a
sort of pastry or baked flour; a particular musical
air [cf. मण्ठक]; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people,
(also read मन्दक; cf. मण्डिक.)

मण्डन, अस्, आ, अम्, adorning, dressing out,
decorating; fond of ornament; (अस्), m., N. of a
man, = मण्डन-मिश्र below; (अम्), n. the act
of adorning or decorating, bedecking one's self, de-
coration, jewels, trinkets, (मण्डनं कुरुते, she
adorns herself); ornament, embellishment; N. of a
work.
—मण्डन-कवि, इस्, m., N. of a Pandit.
—मण्डन-मिश्र, अस्, m., N. of a philosopher
(also called Sureśvarācārya and Viśva-rūpācārya).
—मण्डनार्ह (˚न-अर्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, worthy of
ornaments.
मण्डनक in मुख-म्˚, q. v.

मण्डपिक, अस्, m. or मण्डपिका, f. (fr. मण्ड-
प above), a little pavilion; a small shed, shop.

मण्डयन्त, अस्, m. an ornament; an actor; an
assembly of women; food; (ई), f. a woman.

मण्डिक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people; (also read
शुण्डिक.)

मण्डित, अस्, आ, अम्, adorned, ornamented, deco-
rated; (अस्), m. (with Jainas) N. of one of the
eleven Gaṇādhipas; a Vāsiṣṭha.
—मण्डित-पु-
त्र, अस्, m. = मण्डित, N. of one of the eleven
Gaṇādhipas.
मण्डित मण्डित. See col. 1.

मण्डप मण्ड-प. See under मण्ड, p. 731,
col. 3.

माण्डप माण्डप, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मण्डप),
belonging to a temple.

मण्डपूल मण्डपूल, boots with legs, high
boots, jack-boots.

मण्डरी मण्डरी, f. a sort of cricket; [cf.
माण्डरिक.]

मण्डल मण्डल, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be fr.
rt. मण्ड्), round; (अस्), m. a circular array of troops,
an army drawn up in a circle; a species of snake; a
dog; (अम्), n. a disk (especially the disk of the sun
or moon); anything round (e. g. आदर्श-मण्ड-
लम्, a mirror; चाप-मण्डलम्, the circular bend
of a strung bow); a circle, globe, ball, orb, wheel,
circumference, ring, (said to be also अस्, m.); the
path or orbit of a heavenly body; a great circle (in
astronomy); the visible horizon; a halo round the
sun or moon; any circular figure or diagram; a sort
of mystical diagram formed in summoning a divinity,
&c.; a circular bandage (in surgery); a round mark
(as a mark caused by a finger-nail, &c.); a parti-
cular attitude or position of the feet in shooting; a
district, arrondissement, territory, province (sometimes
at the end of modern names as in Coro-mandal, the
whole circle of territory over which one of the twelve
emperors termed Cakra-vartins was supposed to have
reigned in ancient times); a surrounding district or
territory, the circle of a king's near and distant
neighbours (with whom he must maintain political
and diplomatic relations; four or six or ten or even
twelve such neighbouring princes are enumerated);
a multitude, assemblage, group, troop, collection,
band, whole body, association, society, company,
heap; a division of the Ṛg-veda, (the whole Saṃ-
hitā of the Śākala school, which is the only extant
Śākhā or recension of the Ṛg-veda, is divided into
ten Maṇḍalas, and these into 85 Anuvākas or
sections, and these again into 1017, or with the
eleven additional hymns, into 1028 Sūktas or hymns,
which again are divided into 10, 417 Ṛcs or verses,
and these into 153, 826 Padas or words; the other
method of division is into Aṣṭakas, Adhyāyas,
Vargas, Ṛcs, and Padas; cf. वर्ग); a sort of
cutaneous eruption or leprosy with circular spots, (in
this sense also n. pl.); a sugar-ball, sweetmeat; a
sort of perfume (= व्याघ्र-नख); a particular
oblation or sacrifice; (ई), f. a circle, &c.; an assem-
blage, company, corporate body, church, multitude,
crowd; walking round, whirling, circular motion; a
nest; bent grass, Panicum Dactylon (see दूर्वा).
—मण्डल-कार्मुक, अस्, आ, अम्, having a circular
bow or whose bow is bent; [cf. मण्डली-कृत.]
—मण्डल-चिह्न, अम्, n. the sign or mark of a
circle.
—मण्डल-नृत्य, अम्, n. a circular dance
(especially a dance like that said to have been
danced by the Gopīs round Kṛṣṇa and his mistress
Rādhā; also read मण्डली-नृत्य).
—मण्डल-
न्यास, अम्, n. the putting down or drawing a
circle; मण्डल-न्यासं कृ, to describe a circle.
—मण्डल-पत्त्रिका, f. a red-flowering Punar-
navā.
—मण्डल-पुच्छक, अस्, m. a species of
insect.
—मण्डल-ब्राह्मण, अम्, n., N. of an
Upaniṣad.
—मण्डल-भाग, अस्, m. part of a
circle.
—मण्डल-वट, अस्, m. an Indian fig-tree
forming a circle; [cf. मण्डलिन्.]
—मण्डल-वर्-
तिन्, ई, m. the governor of a province, ruler of a
small kingdom; [cf. चक्र-वर्तिन्.]
—मण्डल-
वर्ष, अम्, n. (probably) general rain extending
over a whole country, lasting rain.
—मण्डल-शस्,
ind. by circles, in circles, in rings.
—मण्डलाग्र
(˚ल-अग्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, round-pointed, having a round
point or end; (अस्), m. a bent or rounded sword, a
scimitar, sabre; (अम्), n., scil. शस्त्र, a surgeon's
circular knife.
—मण्डलाधिप or मण्डलाधीश
(˚ल-अध्˚), अस्, m. the lord of a district, ruler or
[]
governor of a province, king of a country, a monarch,
emperor.
—मण्डली-करण, अम्, n. the act of
making round, rounding, gathering in a ball or
circle, coiling, &c.
—मण्डली-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति,
-कर्तुम्, to make round, form into a circle or ball,
form into a ring, coil.
—मण्डली-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्,
formed into a circle, made circular, rounded, curved,
tense, bent (as a bow).
—मण्डली-नृत्य = मण्-
डल-नृत्य, q. v.
—मण्डली-भू, cl. 1. P. -भ-
वति, -भवितुम्, to become round, to form a circle.
—मण्डली-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, become round, be-
come circular or rounded, curved, bent (as a bow).
—मण्डलेश (˚ल-ईश) or मण्डलेश्वर (˚ल-
ईश्˚), अस्, m. the lord of a district, ruler or governor
of a province.
—मण्डलेश-त्व, अम्, n. rulership
of a province, governorship.
—मण्डलोत्तम (˚ल-
उत्˚), अम्, n. the best or most excellent empire,
principal kingdom.

मण्डलक, अम्, n. a disk; a circle; a district,
province; a cutaneous disease, white leprosy with
round spots; a circular array of troops; a group; a
mirror; (अस्), m. a dog.
—मण्डलक-राजन्, आ,
m. the king of a small district or province.

मण्डलय, Nom. P. मण्डलयति, &c., to
make round or circular.

मण्डलाय, Nom. A. मण्डलायते, -यितुम्, to
become a circle, form one's self into a circle or ring,
coil one's self.

मण्डलायमान, अस्, आ, अम्, becoming circular,
forming one's self into a circle or ring, coiling one's
self.

मण्डलायित, अस्, आ, अम्, formed into a circle or
ring; round, circular, = वर्तुल?; (अम्), n. a ball,
globe.

मण्डलित, अस्, आ, अम्, made round or circular,
(परि-मण्डलित, rounded, whirled round.)
—मण्-
डलित-हस्त-काण्ड, अस्, m. having a trunk formed
in rings or circles (said of an elephant).

मण्डु मण्डु, उस्, m., N. of a Ṛṣi; [cf.
माण्डव्य.]
मण्डुक in पङ्क-म्˚, q. v.

मण्डूक मण्डूक, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt.
मण्ड्), a frog; N. of a particular breed of horses;
the plant Calosanthes Indica; N. of a Ṛṣi; of a
Nāga; (according to some) = गाढ-तेजस्?; (आ),
f. the plant Rubia Munjista, = मञ्जिष्ठा; (ई), f.
a female frog; N. of several plants (= मण्डूक-
पर्णी); Hydrocotyle Asiatica; Polanisia Icosandra;
Clerodendrum Siphonanthus; a particular shrub (com-
monly called Khulakuḍī); a wanton woman; (अम्),
n. a kind of coitus; (if मण्डूक occurs at the end of
an adj. comp. the fem. ends in आ.)
—मण्डूक-कुल,
अम्, n. a collection or assemblage of frogs.
—मण्-
डूक-गति-लालस, अस्, आ, अम्, ardently desiring the
gait of a frog.
—मण्डूक-पर्ण, अस्, m., N. of
several plants, Calosanthes Indica, = कपीतन; (ई),
f. Rubia Munjista; Clerodendrum Siphonanthus;
Polanisia Icosandra; Hydrocotyle Asiatica; a par-
ticular shrub (commonly called Khulakuḍī).
—मण्-
डूकपर्णिका, f. = मण्डूक-पर्णी.
—मण्डूक-
प्लुति, इस्, f. ‘frog-leap,’ the passing over or skipping
of several Sūtras and supplying from a previous Sūtra
(in grammar).
—मण्डूक-मातृ, ता, f. ‘the mother
of frogs,’ the plant Clerodendrum Siphonanthus.
—मण्डूक-योग, अस्, m. a particular kind of ab-
stract meditation in which an ascetic sits motionless
like a frog.
—मण्डूकयोग-नियत, अस्, आ, अम्,
intent upon the frog-meditation.
—मण्डूकयोग-
शयन, अम्, n. lying like a frog in deep medita-
tion.
—मण्डूक-शायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, lying like a frog.
—मण्डूक-सरस, अम्, n. a frog-pond, pond
[]
full of frogs [cf. Pāṇ.

].
—मण्डूकानु-
वृत्ति (˚क-अन्˚), इस्, f. ‘frog-course,’ skipping over
or omitting at intervals; [cf. मण्डूक-प्लुति.]

माण्डूक माण्डूक, आस्, m. pl. (fr. मण्डूक),
N. of a school.
—माण्डूकी-पुत्र, अस्, m., N. of a
teacher.

मण्डूर मण्डूर, अम्, n. rust of iron, scoriæ,
dross.
—मण्डूर-धाणिकी, f., Ved. a particular
abusive and indelicate expression.

माणव माणव, अस्, m. a youth, lad, young-
ster, (especially) a young Brāhman; a man, little
man, manikin (used contemptuously); a pearl orna-
ment of sixteen strings [cf. अर्ध-म्˚]; epithet of
one of the nine treasures of the Jainas.

माणवक, अस्, m. a lad or boy not exceeding
sixteen years of age; a little man, dwarf, (माया-
माणवको हरिः, Viṣṇu disguising himself under
the form of a dwarf); a manikin (contemptuously);
a silly or childish man, an ignorant or ridiculous
man, (in the drama used as an epithet of the Vidū-
shaka or jocose friend of the king); a pupil, scholar,
religious student; a pearl ornament of a particular
number of strings (e. g. of sixteen, twenty, or forty-
eight strings); (इका), f. a young girl, damsel, wench;
(अम्), n. = माणवक-क्रीड, a kind of metre, four
times ¯ ˘ ˘ ¯ ¯ ˘ ˘ ¯.
—माणवक-क्रीड, अम्, आ,
n. f. ‘boy's play,’ N. of a kind of metre.
—माण-
वक-क्रीडनक or माणवक-क्रीडितक, अम्, n.
= माणवक-क्रीड.

माणवीन, अस्, आ, अम्, proper for boys or lads,
boyish, childish.

माणव्य, अम्, n. a multitude or company of boys
or lads, boyhood.

माणहल माणहल, आस्, m. pl., N. of a
people.

माणिकाम्बू माणिकाम्बू, ऊस्, f., N. of a
woman, the mother of the Scholiast Viṭṭhala.

माणिक्य माणिक्य, अम्, n. a ruby [cf. रङ्ग-
म्˚]; (अस्), m., N. of a man; (आ), f. a kind of
small house-lizard.
—माणिक्य-चन्द्र, अस्, m., N.
of a king of Tīra-bhukti.
—माणिक्य-मय, अस्, ई,
अम्, made or consisting of rubies.
—माणिक्य-मल्ल,
[]
अस्, m., N. of a king (patron of Manohara-śarman
the commentator on the Śruta-bodha).
—माणिक्य-
मिश्र, अस्, m. a proper N.
—माणिक्य-राय, अस्,
m. a proper N.
—माणिक्य-सूरि, इस्, m., N. of a
Gujarāṭhī author and of other persons.

माणिचर माणिचर, अस्, m., Ved. (accord-
ing to a commentator) the tutelary genius of the
war-chariot.
माणिचार, अस्, m. = माणिभद्र below.
माणिपार माणिपार, अस्, m. a proper N.

माणिपाल माणिपाल, see Gaṇa Mahiṣyādi
to Pāṇ.
माणिपालिक, see Gaṇa Revatyādi to Pāṇ.

माणिबन्ध माणिबन्ध, अम्, n. = माणि-
मन्थ, q. v.

माणिभद्र माणिभद्र = मणि-भद्र, a
king of the Yakṣas.
माणिवर = माणिभद्र above.

माणिमन्थ माणिमन्थ, अम्, n. (fr. मणि-
मन्थ), salt brought from the mountain Maṇi-
mantha, rock-salt, sea-salt.
माणिमन्त, अम्, n. = माणिमन्थ above.

माणिरूप्यक माणिरूप्यक (fr. मणि + रूप्य),
see Pāṇ.

माण्डकर्णि माण्डकर्णि, इस्, m. (a patro-
nymic fr. मण्ड-कर्ण), N. of a Muni.

माण्डरिक माण्डरिक (fr. मण्डर), see
Gaṇa Aṅgulyādi to Pāṇ.

माण्डव माण्डव, अम्, n. (fr. मण्डु), N. of
a Sāman; एडम् माण्डवम्, N. of a Sāman.

माण्डवी, f. (fr. माण्डव्य below), N. of a
daughter of Kuśa-dhvaja and wife of Bharata; a N.
of Dākṣāyaṇī at Māṇḍavya.

माण्डव्य, अस्, m. (fr. मण्डु), a patronymic,
N. of a teacher; (आस्), m. pl. the descendants of
Māṇḍavya; N. of a people; (अस्, अम्), m. or n. (?),
N. of a place.
—माण्डव्य-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a
city on the Godā.
—माण्डव्येश्वर (˚य-ईश्˚), अम्,
n., N. of a Liṅga.
—माण्डव्येश्वर-तीर्थ, अम्,
n., N. of a place of pilgrimage.

माण्डव्यायन, अस्, ई, m. f. (fr. माण्डव्य), a
patronymic (Gaṇa Lohitādi to Pāṇ.

माण्डूकायन, आस्, m. pl., N. of a school.
—माण्-
डूकायनी-पुत्र, अस्, m., N. of a teacher.
माण्डूकायनि, इस्, m., Ved., N. of a preceptor.

माण्डूकि, इस्, m. (fr. मण्डूक), a patronymic
(Pāṇ.

माण्डूकेय, अस्, m. (fr. मण्डूक), a patronymic,
N. of a teacher; (आस्), m. pl. his descendants; (अम्),
n. the doctrine or teaching of Māṇḍūkeya.

माण्डूकेयीय, relating to or connected with Māṇ-
ḍūkeya.

माण्डूक्य, probably an adj. from माण्डूक.
—माण्डूक्य-श्रुति, इस्, f. the Māṇḍukya revela-
tion or teaching.
—माण्डूक्योपनिषद् (˚य-उप्˚),
त्, f., N. of a short but important Upaniṣad of the
Atharva-veda.
